sana: Heads up — priming cache hit-rate for seeded prompts dropped badly after last night's compiler+kernel blend rollout. From ~91% -> ~62% on production traffic for seeding routes. 95p latency up ~18ms. :eyes:
liam: Oof. timeline? which rollout specifically?
sana: Deploy-bot shows rollout window around 02:14 UTC. Kernel selection change: runtime v2.14 with compiler blend flag 'auto_kernel_mix' enabled.
deploy-bot: rolled runtime:v2.14 -> all zones at 2026-03-15T02:14Z (feature: auto_kernel_mix=true) — canary passed.
maria: Any signs in profiler of different KV key bytes or normalization? last time fused-attn changed we saw canonicalization drift.
sana: Quick profiler snapshot attached (excerpt):
```
kv_lookup_total: 1,213,982
kv_lookup_hits: 753,021 (62.0%)
kv_lookup_misses: 460,961 (↑3.4x vs baseline)
kv_key_bytes_hash_variants: 0x1a2b,0x4f9c,0x3c4d (more diversity than usual)
batch_affinity_rebalances: 840 (spike)
```
sana: Also seeing more short-seq requests getting routed to fused-attn kernel. That kernel appears to alter padding/trim behavior for prefix keys.
jon: Sounds like a key canonicalization mismatch. If the kernel changes how it trims trailing padding or rounds fp values before serialization, hash will diverge. Any change to quant profile for keys? int8 vs fp16 mapping can flip a few bytes.
maria: We enabled quant-profile 'compact-keys' in the compile pipeline for v2.14 — that could alter K bytes. We should confirm whether key canonicalizer runs pre- or post-quant.
liam: Can you reproduce with a small batch? if flipping kernel_selection back to legacy restores hit-rate that's a clear signal.
sana: Quick experiment: toggled feature flag kernel_selector=legacy for one shard, got hit-rate -> 89% within 20m. Reverting the flag back to auto_mix drops it again.
jon: That matches canonicalization. Two mitigation options: (1) force legacy kernel for priming routes until we fix canonicalizer, or (2) add a post-compile key-canonicalize step that normalizes bytes across kernel variants.
maria: For option 2 we need a cheap canonicalizer that runs before KV key serialization. Adding cost should be negligible if it's a simple trimming+masking pass. We should also verify that salted keys (per-deploy salt) didn't change between model/compile steps.
liam: Immediate suggestion: add routing override for routes tagged priming=true -> legacy kernel for next 24h and schedule a hotfix to canonicalizer. I'll open a rollout change. :pray:
sana: I've queued a canary and a short dashboard. Link: https://internal.redwood/perf/dashboards/priming-hit/3632109876 (only accessible internally).
jon: I can run a small batch job to diff key bytes before/after kernel serialization and produce a patch for canonicalizer. Will post findings here in ~2h.
maria: Also check model version pinning — if model weights changed quant thresholds, that could affect key precomputation.
sana: Filed a short incident & mitigation: route override -> legacy for priming-heavy routes, patch candidate for canonicalizer in progress. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
liam: Great. once jon posts diffs we'll decide whether to hotfix canonicalizer or revert compile flag.
deploy-bot: feature flag kernel_selector=legacy applied to route-group priming-heavy at 2026-03-15T03:02Z (scope: shard-7).
jon: diff job started (trace id: trace-6b3f). Will update with minimal repro and suggested patch.
sana: putting notes into the incident doc and marking P1 until we have canonicalizer patch or safe rollout plan.
liam: 👍 keep lightweight timeline updates here.
